Manufacturers and suppliers referenced across the
[Equipment](../equipment/index.md) catalog. Aquatic timing comes from a small number
of companies, and the equipment sections here are grouped by manufacturer because
touchpads, start systems, lane speakers, and relay platforms are normally bought to
match a facility's timing console. Each product article records which console or
start system the device connects to.

## What lives here

Each vendor has its own page, and this index links to them. Vendors are referred
to by name, and logos are not reproduced, see
[Sources & citations](../about/sources.md). When citing a vendor's manual, link
to the official copy rather than hosting it.

Vendors are grouped by their main role in the wiki. A company that does several things is
listed once.

## Articles

### Timing and scoring manufacturers

Colorado Time Systems, Daktronics, Swiss Timing, and Seiko are the principal manufacturers of
complete aquatic timing systems, and ALGE-Timing makes one built around its TM-SWIM. International Sports Timing and Superior Swim Timing are smaller United
States makers offering lower-cost alternatives to a full console. Several of the other companies
are recorded only in the swimming press or in the documentation of meet software that reads
their equipment.

| Vendor | Headquarters | Equipment documented here |
|---|---|---|
| [ALGE-Timing](alge-timing.md) | Lustenau, Austria | The TM-SWIM timing console, SWIM 2000 and Timy timers, start units, touchpads, starting platforms and display boards |
| [BestBet](bestbet.md) | Not established | A timing console documented only by comparison with the Colorado Time Systems 4 |
| [Chronomix](chronomix.md) | Sunnyvale, California, United States | A battery-powered eight-lane printing swim timer from 1977 and the nine-lane `CC721` from 1980 |
| [Colorado Time Systems (CTS)](colorado-time-systems.md) | Loveland, Colorado, United States | Timing consoles (System 5, System 6, Gen7), the Championship and Infinity start systems, AquaGrip touchpads, lane speakers, relay-judging platforms, and the DisplayLink display software |
| [Daktronics](daktronics.md) | Brookings, South Dakota, United States | OmniSport timing consoles, T-7000 touchpads, the HS-200 Horn Start, RTOP relay platforms, lane speakers, and scoreboards |
| [Incomar](incomar.md) | Utica, Michigan, United States | The Splash I pacing system of 1980, and a console Hy-Tek supported in 1988 |
| [International Sports Timing (IST)](international-sports-timing.md) | Grand Rapids, Michigan, United States | The SWIMSTART start system and an under-block speaker system |
| [Kyrotech](kyrotech.md) | Northbrook, Illinois, United States | The Tec-Timer printing meet timer, advertised in the press between 1984 and 1993, and the AutoCoach pace clock, advertised 1982–1986 |
| [Macsha](macsha.md) | Not established | The Macsha Swim touchpad and lane-unit system |
| [Microgate](microgate.md) | Bolzano, Italy | No equipment; the owner of ALGE-Timing |
| [Microplus](microplus.md) | Marene, Italy | No equipment; data processing at the 2014 European swimming championships |
| [Nevco](nevco.md) | Edwardsville, Illinois, United States | Aquatic timing and scoring systems built on ALGE-Timing equipment |
| [Seiko](seiko.md) | Tokyo, Japan | PS-series electronic starters and the AQUA and Full-Frame touch plates |
| [Sportronic](sportronic.md) | Germany | A swimming timing system with an STM-11 control unit, and transponder lap counting |
| [Stramatel](stramatel.md) | Le Cellier, France | The Aquasport V swim timer, Aquaswim software and Aquatouch touchpads |
| [Superior Swim Timing (SST)](superior-swim-timing.md) | United States | Laptop-based timing software, the Atlantis start system, and lane speakers and harnesses |
| [Swiss Timing](swiss-timing.md) | Corgémont, Switzerland | Quantum Aquatics, ARES 21 and OSM timing consoles, StartTime starting devices, in-block loudspeakers, the OBL2 Pro backstroke ledge and Calypso scoreboards, sold under the Omega brand |
| [Take Your Mark](take-your-mark.md) | Not established | A timing console reached by shared file rather than by cable |

| [Wylas Timing](wylas-timing.md) | Not established | A wireless timing system for six to ten lanes, with its own screen displays |

### Federations

The DSV publishes the [DSV-Standard](../software/file-formats/dsv-standard.md), which was written in
its regional association for North Rhine-Westphalia.

| Vendor | Headquarters | Equipment documented here |
|---|---|---|
| [Deutscher Schwimm-Verband (DSV)](deutscher-schwimm-verband.md) | Kassel, Germany | No equipment; the German swimming federation, publisher of the DSV-Standard data format |
| [Schwimmverband NRW](schwimmverband-nrw.md) | North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany | No equipment; the regional association, formerly the WSV, in which the DSV-Standard was written |

Colorado Time Systems was founded in 1972 and Daktronics in 1968. Swiss Timing is
part of the Swatch Group, Seiko traces its origins to 1881, IST has supplied aquatics
facilities since 1992, SST was founded in 2010, and FINIS in 1993.

More manufacturers are added as equipment is documented.
